name: Visa Exemption for Tourism (30 days)
summary: Citizens of the listed countries can enter Thailand for tourism without a visa and stay up to 30 days. This replaced the old 60-day exemption on Sep 15, 2026. Tourism only.

other: Ordinary passports only.

The 60-country list is from the Department of Consular Affairs document dated Sep 15, 2026. An earlier May 2026 summary said 54 countries, so check the official list before relying on a specific country.
Each country gets only one exemption scheme. The old 60-day scheme was cancelled for all 93 countries.
People already in Thailand under the old rules can stay until their permitted period ends.

Nationalities not on this list or the bilateral list need a visa through the e-visa system. News reports say 21 nationalities lost visa-free entry, but I could not confirm that list on an official page.

stay.note: Extension rules not confirmed on an official page.

steps: Submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) before you fly.
Show your passport at immigration on arrival.

name: Visa Exemption for Tourism (15 days)
summary: A new 15-day tourism exemption started Sep 15, 2026 for a small group of countries. The official sources I read do not fully agree on which ones.

other: Ordinary passports only.
The Sep 15, 2026 15-day list names Seychelles and Mauritius. The May 2026 summary also put Maldives here, but the Sep 15 30-day list includes Maldives. Check the official list.

name: Bilateral Visa Exemption Agreements
summary: Some countries have their own visa-free agreements with Thailand. Stay length follows each agreement.

other: A May 2026 MFA summary lists 90 days for China, Hong Kong, Kazakhstan, Laos, Macao, Mongolia, Russia, Timor-Leste and Vietnam. It lists 30 days for Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Peru and South Korea, and 14 days for Cambodia and Myanmar (Myanmar at international airports only).
A later MFA summary was garbled and I could not confirm those durations. Check the official bilateral list.

name: Visa on Arrival
summary: Only a few nationalities can still get a visa on arrival, for up to 15 days. It was cut from 31 countries to a handful on Sep 15, 2026.

other: Ordinary passports only.
The Sep 15, 2026 DCA page lists Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia. The May 2026 summary listed India as a fourth, but India is on the 30-day exemption list in the Sep 15 document.

name: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC)
summary: Every non-Thai traveler must fill out the free online arrival card before entering Thailand, by air, land or sea. Submit it no more than 3 days before you arrive.

other: Required for infants and children too.
Not required for crew, technical landings, or transit passengers who do not pass through immigration. If you leave the airport you need one.
The page says no fee. Only use the official site, tdac.immigration.go.th.

steps: Fill in your passport, trip and stay details.
Submit it within 3 days before arrival and keep the confirmation.

name: Tourist Visa (TR1) via e-Visa
summary: If your country is not on the visa-free or visa-on-arrival lists, apply for a tourist visa online. Choose single or multiple entry.

savings.note: Minimum funds shown for tourist visas.

other: Needs a travel booking and proof of accommodation.
Approval is at the officer's discretion, and extra documents or an interview can be asked for.
Visa fee and exact validity rules were not on the page I read. Check thaievisa.go.th for the current fee.
News reports say 21 nationalities now need a visa after Sep 15, 2026. I could not confirm that list on an official page.

stay.note: Visa is valid 3 or 6 months. Length of each stay is set at entry and was not confirmed here.

steps: Upload passport page, photo, funds proof, booking and accommodation proof.
Pay the fee online and wait for the decision.

name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa: Wealthy Global Citizen
summary: A 10-year visa for people with at least USD 1 million in assets and USD 500,000 already invested in Thailand. It is granted for 5 years and extended for 5 more.

savings.note: Global or Thai assets in your own name.

investment.note: Thai government bonds with 5+ years left, direct investment in Thai-registered companies, or Thai property. Must be made before applying.

other: Need health insurance of at least USD 50,000, Thai social security, or USD 100,000 in a bank account for 12+ months.
All conditions must be kept for the life of the visa.

name: Permanent Residence (Residence Permit)
summary: Thailand grants a limited number of permanent residence permits each year, with a quota per nationality. You need 3 straight years on a Non-Immigrant visa with one-year extensions.

other: Categories: investment, employment, humanitarian (family), expert, and other special cases.
Investment: at least 10 million THB remitted into Thailand.
Employment: 3 years on a work permit, 1 year with the current company, and either 80,000 THB a month for 2 years or tax returns showing 100,000 THB a year.
Spouse of a Thai: about 30,000 THB a month average over 2 years. For applicants 50+ it is 65,000 THB a month.
Expert: bachelor's degree or higher, endorsed by the relevant authority, and 3 years of relevant service.
Quotas apply per nationality and the Minister can refuse an otherwise eligible applicant.
Fees and the yearly application window were not on a page I could open. Check immigration.go.th.
